public_rationale: The research documents alignment failures, useful improvements and limits on particular safety methods. None establishes that LLMs alone can never solve alignment, and none supplies an independently validated general solution. The forecast has no deadline, so the absence of a solution by October 28, 2026 cannot count as confirmation.
limitations: Alignment and LLMs alone remain underspecified.
Company experiments establish results within their tested settings.
A search cannot establish the nonexistence of every possible solution.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that LLM-based methods cannot by themselves produce AI that reliably follows intended human goals and safety constraints across relevant deployment settings.
Solve means a robust solution, rather than improved results on selected safety tests.
Alone restricts the proposed solution's technical scope; it is not a separate future antecedent that must occur before the claim can be evaluated.
Ordinary training data, human-specified goals and LLM-based feedback are not automatically excluded. A solution depending on a separate non-LLM mechanism would not falsify this claim.
criteria.support_condition: An independently validated impossibility result establishes that the relevant class of LLM-based methods cannot solve alignment under assumptions matching the ordinary reading.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A publicly documented, independently validated solution achieves reliable alignment using LLM-based methods alone across the relevant deployment settings.

evidence.explanation: Constitutional AI demonstrates progress using model feedback and human-written principles. Improved harmlessness is not an independently validated solution to the full alignment problem.
The experiment demonstrates a specific alignment failure under a constructed training scenario. It does not establish that future LLM-based methods cannot solve alignment.

evidence.explanation: The authors distinguish improvements on targeted evaluations from wider generalization, while also reporting more promising interventions. Neither the failures nor the improvements settle a claim of permanent impossibility.

evidence.explanation: The results concern external filtering under specified computational assumptions. They do not rule out alignment methods that change an LLM's internal architecture or weights.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independently validated LLM-only alignment solution would contradict the claim. A validated impossibility theorem covering that entire class under matching assumptions would support it.
